requirements.REQ_PROVIDER: Real Terraform Plugin Framework provider exposes exactly the ten documented managed resources.
requirements.REQ_STATE: Terraform Core owns durable state and stable identities derive from external object keys rather than mutable desired attributes.
requirements.REQ_REFRESH: Read observes native Linux state without Ansible side effects and makes external drift actionable.
requirements.REQ_UPDATE: Create/Update publish new state only after successful mutation; failed updates preserve the last successful state and retries converge.
requirements.REQ_DELETE: Delete completes only after successful scoped teardown; failures retain management and sibling ownership is preserved.
requirements.REQ_COPY: Copy uses source_digest for source-content changes and observes destination content.
requirements.REQ_TEXT: Named line/block resources are exact, idempotent, side-effect-free on Read and independently owned.
requirements.REQ_IDENTITY: User/group resources observe native account state and preserve stable identity across mutable changes.
requirements.REQ_RUNNER: Runner uses structured argv, propagates non-zero/timeout/cancellation failures and cleans ephemeral playbooks.
requirements.REQ_NORMALIZE: Equivalent modes, unordered values and defaults converge to stable canonical representations.
requirements.REQ_CRON: Cron omitted user/schedule fields converge to root/wildcards, stay clean and preserve named siblings.

prior_evidence.classification_observation: The two NOP-passing behaviors were template variable-map order stability and symlink-target preservation on destroy; their assertions are unchanged and are now classified P2P.

empirical_gate.note: The assertions are unchanged, but the renamed current test identities require a fresh exact-commit deterministic rerun before freeze.
